description:
Site: crate-jmap-chat-types/src/message.rs:492-542 (Message::new constructor).

The chat-types Message::new constructor takes 13 positional args, of
which 4 are zero-valued containers (vec![], vec![], vec![],
HashMap::new()) and the remaining 9 are 'required' but several
(e.g. attachments, mentions, actions, reactions) are routinely empty
on first construction.

The canonical extension-types sibling, jmap-mail-types::Email::new
(crate-jmap-mail-types/src/email.rs:352-393), takes ONLY 6 args —
the truly-required fields per RFC 8621 — and internally defaults
every empty collection and every optional metadata field to its
zero value. Callers then assign optional fields via struct-update
after construction.

Per workspace AGENTS.md "Canonical Templates", jmap-mail-types
is the canonical extension-types template and chat-types must
mirror its shape. Message::new at 13 args is drift from that
canonical.

Per chat-types AGENTS.md 'Constructors' policy:
'Minimal ::new() and named alternates where they enforce a type
invariant ... or absorb required-field boilerplate that callers
would otherwise repeat for every struct ... Otherwise prefer
struct-literal construction.'

Empty Vec<Attachment> / Vec<Mention> / Vec<MessageAction> /
HashMap<String, Reaction> are not type-invariant requirements;
they are 'this field defaulted to empty' assertions. They belong
in the body of new() not the signature.

Recommended fix: shrink Message::new to the truly-required wire
fields per draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00 §Message:
   pub fn new(
       id: Id,
       sender_msg_id: Id,
       sender_id: SenderId,
       chat_id: Id,
       body: impl Into<String>,
       body_type: impl Into<String>,
       sent_at: UTCDate,
       received_at: UTCDate,
       delivery_state: DeliveryState,
   ) -> Self

…with attachments / mentions / actions / reactions defaulted in
the body. Existing callers (one: chat-server message.rs:470)
remove the four empty-container args.

Engineering basis:

- jmap-mail-types Email::new is the canonical pattern; chat-types
  has drifted.
- The 4 'empty vec' args at the call site contribute the most to
  the 'positional-arg slot confusion' risk that JMAP-x2gd.32 flags
  for the call-site review.
- Sole production caller is single-edit-of-known-shape; not a
  propagation hazard.

Scope: chat-types reshape + chat-server call-site update. Test
fixtures in chat-types tests/ (message_deser_minimal etc.) test
deserialize round-trip, not the constructor, so they are unaffected.

Background: JMAP-x2gd.32 closed the chat-server-local part of this
finding (the std::collections::HashMap::new() fully-qualified path);
this is the wider type-design half referenced in .32's description
('the wider Message::new shape lives in jmap-chat-types and would
need a propagation bead there').
title: chat-types Message::new takes 13 positional args; canonical mail-types Email::new takes 6 — drift from canonical extension-types template
